column1: # WVO 5551 (Jan van Nassau to Willem van Oranje, Keulen, 17 April 1574), p3 top, the two cipher lines only
# (WVO's own "Twee regels in cijferschrift"; TX-WV5551D, 25 Sept 2026, from images/05551_p3.jpg re-rendered at
# 300dpi from the WVO PDF, reconciled against a blind Sonnet subagent pass on the same crop). Format: tools/decode_key.py
# 'tsv' (line pos token conf), clear_prefix '=', same style as ciphertext_5549_ps.tsv in this folder.
# Reconciliation: all 32 numeral codes agree 32/32 between this worker's own pass and the independent blind
# subagent pass (both re-verified at 4-8x zoom). The clear (non-cipher) words do not: pos L1-11 "van"/"von"
# (semantically equivalent, kept as "van"), L1-19 "jhro" vs subagent's "zu" (unresolved, token left "=?"),
# L2-9 "vff" vs subagent's "possibly not a word at all" (kept as "vff", conf "?"), L2-16 "beren"/"veren" vs
# subagent's "Perm" (unresolved, token left "=?"). None of these four are cipher codes; none affects the
# H/C/S/M/I/U grade counts below (clear tokens grade "clear"). Both readers agree the last word of each line
# is genuinely cut off by the leaf's own torn/deckled right edge, not just hard to read.
# JVN-GLY, 10 Oct 2026 (PREREG-JVN-GLY.md, gate passed, Opus reader, controls X1/X2/X5 + and X4/X6 - all passed): two clear
# glyphs added on L2 at conf M -- long-s "=ſ" before 104 and Kurrent "=ch" between 104 and 146 ("offentli[vff?] ſ[104]ch"). L2
# positions after 9 shift by +1 (before 104) and +2 (after 104): old L2-16 is now L2-18, old L2-19 now L2-21.
